KnowledgeArticle.Title: Fire Hydrant Complaint
KnowledgeArticle.Description: Report a fire hydrant that is leaking, running, missing, misused, or damaged (including fender post), or blocked by a vehicle.

Section.Name: Fire Hydrant Complaint Intro
Section.Content:
Need something else?

  • Park Maintenance Complaint for hydrants in a park
  • Fire Hydrant Request for a hydrant spray cap or fender post
  • Fire Hydrant Commercial Use Permit
  • Blocked Sidewalk or Street to report a hydrant blocked on the sidewalk or street blocked by an object or activity

You can report a fire hydrant that:

  • Is leaking or running
  • Is damaged or missing
  • Is missing a valve box cover
  • Is being misused
  • Has a damaged fender protection post
  • Is blocked by a vehicle

Section.Name: Leaking or Running
Section.Content:
You can report a fire hydrant that is leaking, running, or running at full blast.

Section.Name: Damaged or Missing
Section.Content:
You can report a fire hydrant that is damaged, broken, cracked, leaning, knocked over, or missing.

Section.Name: Missing Valve Box Cover
Section.Content: You can report a fire hydrant valve box cover that is missing. The valve box is in the street near the hydrant.

ContentAction.Name: Missing Fire Hydrant Valve Box Cover

Section.Name: Misuse
Section.Content: You must have a permit to open a hydrant and use the water for any reason. You can get a ticket for using a hydrant without a permit.

Section.Name: Fender Protection Post Damaged
Section.Content:
The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) installs and maintains fire hydrant fender protection posts based on the type of hydrant and its location.

You can report a fender that is:

  • Damaged
  • Cracked
  • Broken
  • Leaning
  • Knocked over

Section.Name: Blocked by a Vehicle
Section.Content:
You can report a non-emergency vehicle or motorcycle blocking a fire hydrant. 

It is illegal to park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.

If possible, include in your report the vehicle's:

  • Color
  • Make
  • Model
  • License plate number

What Happens Next

Officers from your local police precinct will respond when they are not handling emergency situations.
